[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Wiggle Sort II** [LC 324 · Wiggle Sort II](https://leetcode.com/problems/wiggle-sort-ii/){difficulty="Medium"}

Deal the larger half of the values into the odd slots (the peaks) and the smaller half into the even slots (the valleys). Every comparison then holds with $\ge$; it can only fail by equality, when copies of the middle value land next to each other. Dealing both halves in decreasing order pushes those copies to opposite ends of the array, and then they can meet only if the middle value occurs so often that no answer exists. A median, a three-way partition read through the index map $t \mapsto (1+2t) \bmod (n \mid 1)$, gives the same arrangement in $O(n)$ time and $O(1)$ extra memory.

[Solved in full in @sec-part-p4-a.]{.card-link}

:::
